about: A made-up player's library for trying UpNext without a real one (`upnext mock-library`). The games are real, their details are written by hand and approximate, and the playtimes, dates, statuses and profile belong to nobody. m is minutes played, d days since last played, h HowLongToBeat's main story in hours, c Steam store categories (only some games have them), sc review-tag scales, as aspects (+ praised, - criticized, ~ divisive).

games.says: Praised for a deep one-more-turn loop and endless replay with different leaders. Complaints: a weak late game, AI that cheats, and paid DLC for core features.
Praised for emergent space stories and empire building. Complaints: a steep start, late-game slowdown, and many DLCs.
Praised for the most satisfying automation loop there is and rock-solid performance. Complaints: it eats whole weekends.
Praised for tight combat, a story told across runs and superb voice work. Complaints: late upgrades take some grinding.
Praised for an easy idea with a huge skill ceiling and quick matches. Complaints: toxic players and the store.
Praised for great co-op, friendly players and fair paid cosmetics. Complaints: solo play is weaker.
Praised for a fiendishly addictive poker roguelike that hooks in minutes. Complaints: luck can decide a run.
Praised for warm, funny dialogue and a gorgeous forest. Complaints: an ending that splits people.
Praised for inventive vignettes and a moving family story. Complaints: very short for the price.
Praised for a haunting atmosphere and clever, wordless puzzles. Complaints: short, and an ending that puzzles some.
Praised for its stark look and tense puzzles. Complaints: some trial-and-error deaths.
Praised for stunning watercolour art and music. Complaints: light gameplay.
Praised for a wordless, moving pilgrimage and its quiet online companions. Complaints: two hours long.
Praised for natural dialogue and a creepy radio mystery. Complaints: slow walking between scenes.
Praised for brilliant puzzles, sharp humour and a great co-op campaign. Complaints: hard to find anything wrong.
Praised for tight, chess-like tactics where every move is visible. Complaints: little story.
Praised for precise controls, clever levels and a moving story about anxiety. Complaints: some late screens feel unfair.
Praised for pure deduction and a unique look. Complaints: the art style tires some eyes.
Praised for turning paperwork into tense moral choices. Complaints: repetitive by design.
Praised for a gripping card game that keeps reinventing itself. Complaints: the last act drags.
Praised for superb quests, characters and a huge world. Complaints: clunky combat and an overwhelming map of markers.
Praised for an astonishing world and a moving story. Complaints: a slow start, heavy controls and long chores.
Praised for thrilling machine fights and a striking world. Complaints: stiff side quests.
Praised since the 2.0 update for its city, characters and main story. Complaints: launch-era bugs that still linger.
Praised for a strange, meditative delivery loop and a striking world. Complaints: a very slow start.
Praised for style, music and a cast you grow to love. Complaints: over a hundred hours with a slow opening.
Praised for a gripping crime story and absurd side quests. Complaints: random street fights get repetitive.
Praised for a gorgeous ancient Greece. Complaints: level gates that push grinding and a bloated quest list.
Praised for companions and banter. Complaints: filler fetch quests in the first area that drag on.
Praised for huge, satisfying hunts with friends. Complaints: farming parts for gear and a confusing start.
Praised for great bosses and level design. Complaints: punishing for newcomers.
Praised for thrilling sword fights. Complaints: early walls like Genichiro stop many players.
Praised for exploration and settlement building. Complaints: thin dialogue choices and bugs.
Praised as a once-in-a-lifetime mystery best played knowing nothing. Complaints: fiddly flying and a horror-ish late area.
Praised for an endlessly surprising open world. Complaints: stutters on PC and a brutal late game.
Praised for a thrilling, scary ocean to explore. Complaints: inventory juggling.
Praised for tense, grim expeditions and a great narrator. Complaints: the late game turns into a grind.
Praised for a vast, beautiful underground kingdom and tight combat. Complaints: some long walks back after dying.
Praised for the best writing in games and a detective full of voices. Complaints: almost no combat, lots of reading.
Praised for the deckbuilder that defined the genre, endlessly replayable. Complaints: dated art.
Praised for tense starship runs full of tough calls. Complaints: brutal luck.
Praised for a calm, flexible daily loop of farming, fishing and friendships. Complaints: a slow first week.
Praised for a soothing tile-laying puzzle. Complaints: runs feel alike after a while.
Praised for a charming little island and warm writing. Complaints: over in an afternoon.
Praised for telling a life through the things in boxes. Complaints: short.
Praised for rule-bending puzzles that make you feel clever. Complaints: some later levels are brutal.
Praised for a cute, dark mix of cult management and dungeon runs. Complaints: thin combat over time.
Praised as a story generator where every colony goes wrong differently. Complaints: pricey DLC.
Praised for a bleak city builder full of hard moral choices. Complaints: short scenarios.
Praised for tense squad tactics. Complaints: a strict timer and long load times.
Praised for inventive turn-based fights and co-op freedom. Complaints: a weaker last act.
Praised for choices that matter and a memorable cast. Complaints: act 3 performance.
Praised for a beloved trilogy with choices that carry over. Complaints: the first game's driving and combat show their age.
Praised for a strange, brutalist office and great powers. Complaints: a cryptic story and frame drops.
Praised for relentless, joyful shooting and a pounding soundtrack. Complaints: multiplayer is an afterthought.
Praised for one of the best shooter campaigns, with inventive levels. Complaints: short.
Praised as a classic with clever physics puzzles. Complaints: some vehicle sections drag.
Praised for a space station full of creative solutions. Complaints: weak gunplay and enemies.
Praised for brilliant levels like the Clockwork Mansion. Complaints: launch performance.
Praised for a powerful look at psychosis and binaural sound. Complaints: repetitive puzzles.
Praised for a terrifying police station and a relentless stalker. Complaints: the second run repeats a lot.
Praised as one of the scariest games, with no way to fight back. Complaints: dated visuals.
Praised for constant dread. Complaints: jump scares wear thin.
Praised for ghost hunts with friends that are scary and funny. Complaints: thin solo play.
Praised for dense, haunting survival horror. Complaints: a cryptic story.
Praised for constantly changing co-op ideas. Complaints: the story's tone grates on some.
Praised for viking co-op building and exploring. Complaints: farming materials gets tedious.
Praised for enormous content for the price. Complaints: you'll need the wiki.
Praised for a cozy, tearful game about saying goodbye. Complaints: busywork in the middle.
Praised for secrets hidden in an in-game manual. Complaints: tough boss fights.
Praised for crisp combat and a melancholy crow's tale. Complaints: little to do after the end.
Praised for slick one-hit kills and a twisting story. Complaints: ends on a cliffhanger.
Praised for brutal, fast restarts and a great soundtrack. Complaints: erratic enemy AI.
Praised for gorgeous 1930s animation and tough bosses. Complaints: very hard.
Praised for elegant subway puzzles in minutes. Complaints: ends the same way every time.
Praised for a calm, minimalist builder. Complaints: little variety.
Praised for haunting, literary storytelling. Complaints: slow and opaque.
Praised for a rich historical mystery where you never learn the truth. Complaints: lots of walking and reading.
Praised for tender writing about precarious life on a space station. Complaints: easy once you have money.
Praised for wild deckbuilding combos across three floors. Complaints: a bland story.
Praised for an odd, hypnotic loop. Complaints: grinding resources between runs.
Praised for a city builder that never goes stale. Complaints: a lot to learn.
Praised for a fresh mix of RTS and city building. Complaints: AI that's easy to beat.
Praised for deep city building and mods. Complaints: traffic AI and big-city slowdowns.
Praised for silly diseases and Theme Hospital charm. Complaints: later levels feel samey.
Praised as oddly relaxing long drives across Europe. Complaints: map DLCs add up.
Praised for huge fantasy battles and varied factions. Complaints: many DLCs.
Praised for cheap, chaotic fun in 30-minute runs. Complaints: it plays itself.
Praised for sharp jokes and fair puzzles. Complaints: an ending some dislike.
Praised for honest writing about coming home. Complaints: slow days that repeat.
Praised for quick, chaotic arena runs. Complaints: runs blur together.
Praised for building huge factories in a beautiful world. Complaints: it swallows weekends.

games.n: Ori and the Will of the Wisps
games.says: Praised for breathtaking art and fluid movement. Complaints: some launch bugs.
Praised for sandbox levels full of absurd ways to kill. Complaints: always-online and a messy menu.
Praised for a profound story told across several playthroughs and an incredible soundtrack. Complaints: a poor PC port.
Praised for a bleak train journey across Russia. Complaints: stiff voice acting.
Praised for exploring anywhere and endless mods. Complaints: floaty combat and old bugs.
Praised for a quiet story found in an empty house. Complaints: short and slight.
Praised for translating an ancient language yourself. Complaints: slow sailing.
Praised for kung fu that feels earned and an ageing twist on death. Complaints: a harsh difficulty curve and a camera that fights you in tight rooms.
Praised for lightsaber combat and big planets to explore. Complaints: stutter and crashes on PC at launch, better since.
Praised for production chains that hook for hours and a lovely busy harbour. Complaints: the Ubisoft launcher and a lot of paid DLC.
Praised for a grim, handsome world and satisfying combat in the campaign. Complaints: a thin endgame, always online, and seasons that reset progress.
Praised for its ink-wash art, a warm story and the brush that draws on the world. Complaints: a slow opening and a lot of talk.
Praised for a dread-soaked world and fights that reward patience. Complaints: punishing deaths and a few cheap bosses.

routines.name: Saturday co-op
routines.note: Voice chat on, two or three of us

second_player.about: A second player on the same computer with a small Steam account of their own: three games player 1 has too, with their own hours, and three only they own (only), which player 1 sees as never played. hidden_by_first are games player 1 hid from everyone else.
second_player.name: Sam
